note: The whole ramp as one prop: three cells (21 studs), road surface 7.07 at the origin cell's -X edge descending to 0.07 at +X so the toe lands on the street tile. highway-kit is generated by tools/assets/highway_kit.py and authored in STUDS, so scale is 1.0 and every pos is studs. Origin = bottom centre of the cell at ground level; road surface 7.07 (= CityDressing highway.deckHeight), soffit 6.10 (contract floor 6.0), parapet top 7.87. The deck is 7.14 wide: it cantilevers 0.07 past the cell on its free edges - testfit reports that as exceeding the 7x7 footprint, it is the fascia overhang and is deliberate - and stops at exactly 3.5 on any edge that butts a neighbouring cell. Grade is 1:2.64 for the first 16 studs, then a parabola landing tangent to the street. The girder keeps its 0.97 depth until the soffit reaches the ground near x 12.6, from where the ramp is a solid embankment. Cells 1 and 2 are carried by ramp piers whose cap top is cut to the same grade (a flat cap leaves a wedge of daylight uphill); each is dropped by slope * (x + 3.5) so the cap meets the soffit, and its shaft is authored below ground so the foot never shows. Cell 3 needs no pier: it is already on the ground.
